title: Kartoon Studios Advances IP-Focused Strategy with Sale of Frederator Channel Network Business
body_text: Kartoon Studios Advances IP-Focused Strategy with Sale of Frederator Channel Network Business Download as PDF July 17, 2026 Company Retains Key Frederator Studios IP For Licensing Opportunities Strategic Transaction Continues Company’s Realignment Towards the Monetization of Premium Intellectual Property BEVERLY HILLS, Calif., July 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kartoon Studios, Inc. (NYSE American: TOON) ("Kartoon Studios" or the "Company"), a global entertainment company creating, producing, distributing and licensing children's and family content, today announced the strategic sale of Frederator Networks' Channel Network business in an all-cash transaction. Kartoon Studios will retain key intellectual property of Frederator Studios, including Bee and PuppyCat , Bravest Warriors , Castlevania and Catbug , for distribution and product licensing opportunities. The strategic sale advances Kartoon Studios' ongoing strategy to align its operating structure and resources on monetization of premium intellectual property, franchise development, animation production, global distribution and consumer-products commercialization. “The transaction separates two businesses with different operating models, margin profiles and growth priorities,” commented Andy Heyward, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Kartoon Studios. “Key to this transaction, we are retaining key intellectual property of Frederator Studios, its creative talent and core properties, along with key channels that support our franchises. We believe this transaction makes Kartoon Studios a more focused company and better positions our team to continue executing on our strategic realignment towards the monetization of premium intellectual property.” Total cash consideration paid to Kartoon Studios totaled $500,000 for the Frederator Networks' Channel Network business. About Kartoon Studios Kartoon Studios (NYSE American: TOON) is a global, vertically integrated children’s and family entertainment company turning owned and controlled intellectual property into enduring, multi-platform franchises. The Company develops, produces, distributes, licenses and monetizes content across the full value chain, creating multiple revenue opportunities and long-term brand value. Kartoon Studios’ growth portfolio includes Hundred Acre Wood and the Stan Lee Universe, alongside established brands and an extensive programming library. The Company operates Mainframe Studios and Toon Media Networks, as well as Beacon Media Group, a full-service marketing, communications, and media agency subsidiary of Kartoon Studios focused on children and family. Together, these assets provide production capabilities, direct audience access and distribution across linear television, AVOD, SVOD, FAST channels and streaming platforms in more than 60 territories. Kartoon Studios is focused on converting its intellectual property, infrastructure and global reach into scalable franchise growth and long-term shareholder value. For more information, visit www.kartoonstudios.com . Forward-looking statements include statements concerning the strategic transaction continuing the Company’s realignment towards the monetization of premium intellectual property; the strategic sale advancing Kartoon Studios' ongoing strategy to align its operating structure and resources on monetization of premium intellectual property, franchise development, animation production, global distribution and consumer-products commercialization and the transaction making Kartoon Studios a more focused company and better positioning its team to continue executing on our strategic realignment towards the monetization of premium intellectual property Words such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “continue,” “could,” “estimate,” “expect,” “forecast,” “intend,” “may,” “plan,” “potential,” “project,” “should,” “will” and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements, although not all forward-looking statements contain these identifying words. title: US ORR-Based Oncology Approvals, DoR Under 6 Months: 2021–2026
summary: FDA oncology approvals (July 2021–2026) where ORR was the primary efficacy basis and median duration of response in pivotal population was under 6 months.
body_text: ORR-based US oncology approvals with a duration of response under 6 months (July 2021 to July 2026) Bottom line Among ORR-based US oncology approvals in the last five years, a median duration of response below 6 months is rare . The FDA's evidentiary bar for response-based (especially accelerated) approvals generally rests on responses being durable , so most of these approvals report a median DoR of 6 months or more, or a median that was not reached at data cutoff. In this window we identified one clear case of a response-rate-based oncology approval whose primary-population median DoR was under 6 months: Product Active ingredient Indication (approval type) Approval date ORR Median DoR Pivotal trial KRAZATI + cetuximab adagrasib KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer, after fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy (accelerated approval) 2024-06-21 34% (95% CI 25, 45) 5.8 months (95% CI 4.2, 7.6) Study 849-001 (KRYSTAL-1) 1165 This was an extension of indication for adagrasib, which was first approved (also under accelerated approval, also on ORR and DoR) for KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC in December 2022 1164 1165 . The one clear case: adagrasib (KRAZATI) plus cetuximab in KRAS G12C colorectal cancer The colorectal indication was granted accelerated approval on June 21, 2024, in combination with cetuximab, based on objective response rate and duration of response from Study 849-001. FDA-confirmed figures are an ORR of 34% (95% CI 25, 45) with a median DoR of 5.8 months (95% CI 4.2 to 7.6 months) 1165 . The label states the indication is approved under accelerated approval based on ORR and DoR, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials 1165 . The 5.8-month median sits just under the 6-month line and is a reasonable illustration of a response-based approval where responses were real but comparatively short-lived, an acceptable trade-off given a heavily pretreated, biomarker-defined population with limited alternatives. Why the list is so short: near-misses and the "not reached" pattern Several response-rate-based approvals landed just above the 6-month threshold, which is why a strict reading yields so few qualifying products: Revumenib (REVUFORJ) , relapsed/refractory KMT2A-translocated acute leukemia (2024-11-15): CR+CRh rate 21.2%, median DoR 6.46 months 1158 . Mirvetuximab soravtansine (ELAHERE) , FRα-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (accelerated approval 2022): ORR 31.7%, median DoR 6.9 months 1172 . Zenocutuzumab (BIZENGRI) , NRG1 fusion-positive NSCLC (2024-12-04): ORR 33%, median DoR 7.4 months 1161 . More commonly, ORR-based approvals in this period reported durable responses well beyond 6 months, or a median that had not been reached at analysis: Tisotumab vedotin (TIVDAK) , recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer (accelerated 2021): ORR 24%, median DoR 8.3 months (innovaTV 204) 1167 . Talquetamab (TALVEY) , relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (accelerated 2023): ORR 73%, median DoR 9.5 months (MonumenTAL-1) 1163 . Tarlatamab (IMDELLTRA) , extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (accelerated 2024): ORR 40%, median DoR 9.7 months (DeLLphi-301) 1178 . Trastuzumab deruxtecan (ENHERTU) , HER2 IHC 3+ tissue-agnostic solid tumors (accelerated 2024): ORR 50%, median DoR 9.9 months (DESTINY-PanTumor02) 1174 . Zongertinib (HERNEXEOS) , HER2 (ERBB2)-mutant NSCLC (accelerated 2025): ORR 75%, median DoR 14.1 months (Beamion LUNG-1) 1171 . Belzutifan (WELIREG) , VHL disease-associated tumors (2021): median DoR not reached at analysis 1159 . The pattern is consistent: when FDA accepts response rate as the efficacy basis, the accompanying DoR is usually the reassurance that responses last. A sub-6-month median is the exception, not the rule. Caveats and limitations for reviewers Reporting format varies. Many oncology labels report DoR as a range (for example "1.0+ to 12.3 months") or as the proportion of responders with DoR at or beyond a landmark (for example "76% with DoR ≥ 6 months") rather than a single median. Where the median was not reached or not estimable, the product was not counted as sub-6-month even if a fraction of responders had short-lived responses. Subgroups can be shorter. CNS, exploratory, and biomarker-subset analyses sometimes show shorter DoR than the pivotal population. These do not represent the basis of approval and were excluded. Legacy labels are not new approvals. Keyword screening also surfaced older drugs whose labels were merely revised in the window (for example a 2022 irinotecan/CAMPTOSAR label revision quoting a 5.8-month response duration from its 1990s colorectal data). These are neither new approvals nor new indications and were excluded. Coverage. This analysis is grounded in Drugs@FDA label and review text. Recall depends on how each label phrases its efficacy tables; a reader wanting an exhaustive, indication-by-indication audit (including every hematologic response-duration figure) can ask Rhizome to run a targeted per-product verification.

title: Putting AI at the Heart of the UK Government Research and Data Infrastructure.
summary: The Evolution of Government Research The United Kingdom stands at a unique crossroads as an international research leader, across many domains, but particularly those that shape government research and official data collection. body_text: The Evolution of Government Research The United Kingdom stands at a unique crossroads as an international research leader, across many domains, but particularly those that shape government research and official data collection. With a rapidly evolving artificial intelligence (AI) landscape, ever-greater government engagement with cutting-edge technologies, and robust ethical and usage frameworks being introduced, a new window of opportunity has opened to embed AI at the centre of the nation’s research and statistics collection ecosystem . Clear signals showing the need for change Considering the current public sector research landscape, this is not simply a technical proposition, but also a policy imperative, where methods of data collection are increasingly primed for change. As an example of this, traditional research approaches — long the backbone of evidence-led decision-making — are now under increasing pressure . As highlighted in a recent Financial Times article , statistics agencies are struggling to deploy large-scale surveys that are robust, rich in insight, and consistently reliable year-on-year [1] . The UK’s Office for National Statistics (ONS) is no exception, which has led to political challenge and, in some cases, the removal of official statistical classification. The associated challenges are not insignificant — rising costs, declining response rates, and respondent fatigue all point to a system in need of augmentation, if not transformation. A second FT piece draws further attention to a particularly urgent case — the difficulty of collecting trade data in services [2] . As a services-led economy, the UK relies heavily on accurate, timely data about cross-border services activity — from legal and financial services to software and consulting. Yet this data is notoriously hard to capture using conventional methods, relying heavily on primary research, which is limited in both granularity and responsiveness. Based on recent findings, this suggests that the value of existing research methods is increasingly constrained. If the UK is to maintain its global competitiveness and develop informed trade and investment policies, it must adopt new approaches to understanding the most important facets of the economy . The opportunity for new data sources to be harnessed is immediate. A Bold, AI-Centric Research Approach It is within these use cases, and more widely, that the role for AI-centric research methods is both clear and exciting. Advances in language understanding, observed learning, structured data gathering and deep reading techniques tailored to specific government research contexts offer transformative potential . These technologies can extract, synthesise, and analyse enormous volumes of data from the open web and other digital sources with unprecedented speed and precision. In doing so, they unlock entirely new modes of understanding — methods that are scalable, customisable, and repeatable. Indeed, the presence of official guidelines outlining the practical use of AI for Government purposes implies a growing recognition of its role [3] . Here, the emphasis is on leveraging the power of technology to bolster insight, efficiency and transparency, whilst following ethical principles and acknowledging limitations — as should absolutely be the case. Building on this platform, and our experience of delivering AI data-led assignments for Governments globally, there are several areas where we believe open web sources and curated AI language models can be deployed to deliver new forms of economic insight: · AI can be used to track the development of emerging sectors — such as Synthetic Biology, Quantum Computing, Green Finance and Advanced Materials — all of which are poorly captured by traditional statistical classifications. · It can help policymakers understand how technologies are adopted and diffused across different industries, clusters and regions, providing insight at a much larger scale and a richness of data not possible before. · At the company level, AI methods can identify trade-related activity from its digital footprint , capturing international exposure, global linkages, and perhaps most interestingly, the trading of economically valuable services. · They can also uncover information about supply chains and commercial partnerships, to better understand relationships and embeddedness, by reading corporate websites, filings, and market intelligence. · Perhaps most compellingly, they can offer more holistic assessments of company growth — looking not just at headcount or turnover, but at innovation output, research activities, hiring patterns, regulatory engagement, and even reputational awards. Example UK Government studies which use and advocate AI research methods and data collection techniques These are all examples of areas that have long challenged economists and statisticians, but where AI-powered analysis of open data sources can offer a step change. In some cases there is traction already — sector research being a prime example . We have deployed our AI technologies on hundreds of assignments, in the UK and globally, for the likes of the UK Departments of Science, Technology and Innovation/Business and Trade, the European Commission and Australian Government, to understand presence, scale, competitiveness, beyond existing limitations. These have breached new ground in terms of insight and granularity, informing policy, helping secure investment and to evaluate landmark programmes. As a tech-led research capability, we see this as a genuine opportunity for the UK government, ONS, and other public sector institutions, to lead the world in frontier data collection . AI doesn’t just supplement traditional research — it reshapes what’s possible. Of course, this is not to dismiss the value of conventional methods. Primary research approaches, remain essential tools for understanding causality, sentiment, and the nuanced impacts of change across sectors, and wider society. They offer rich layers of context that are not always available from observed or secondary data. But they must now be part of a blended model — one that integrates AI-powered approaches into our national data infrastructure. Activating the Vision At Glass.AI, we believe deeply in this vision. Our technologies are already helping public sector organisations unlock new kinds of insight from the open web. We deliver this in a way that makes key components accessible to the user — an understanding of the technology, offering interaction with the data and highlighting the provenance of outputs . We hope to be part of the next wave of innovation in official statistics and policy research, working in partnership with institutions like the ONS, to develop AI-powered methods that complement and enhance traditional techniques. Indeed, the ONS’s recent publication of its economics statistics plan (including survey improvements) highlights an acknowledgement that change is coming and opportunities to include new data inputs alongside existing methods of statistic collection[4]. This could be a fantastic platform to propel public sector data collection across the UK. [1] Roula Khalaf, Statistics wrestles with the rising probability of dud data, Financial Times, May 2025, https://www.ft.com/content/1c30ccb5-ca05-4d49-a995-1c5a5540ef57 [2] Delphin Strauss, UK services trade data ‘of limited value’ says statistics regulator, Financial Times, May 2025, https://www.ft.com/content/fcc0db9f-8118-4130-965a-9a9530545733 [3] UK Government Digital Service (2025), Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government, Available from: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government/artificial-intelligence-playbook-for-the-uk-government-html [4] Office for National Statistics(2025), Restoring Confidence, Improving Quality: Our plans for economic statistics and ONS surveys, Available from: https://blog.ons.gov.uk/2025/06/26/restoring-confidence-improving-quality-our-plans-for-economic-statistics-and-ons-surveys/

title: Digital PR for AI visibility: 5 tactics + how to measure
summary: Having a site isn‘t enough to get AI to talk about you. Use these 5 digital PR tactics to grow AI visibility.
body_text: Digital public relations (PR) helps improve AI visibility by building the internet’s entire record of your brand, which AI search platforms rely on to learn about you. These platforms don’t just rely on what your site says about your brand. That’s because these claims, on their own, can seem unverified or self-serving. But they become more worthy of mentions when trusted third-party sources corroborate them. Investing in digital PR is increasingly important as AI search platforms replace Google as people’s first stop for answers. Here’s the proof that makes digital PR a viable AI visibility strategy, and five tactics to apply to start growing your brand’s AI mentions and citations today. AI search platforms read the internet to learn about you, not just your site AI search platforms read the entire internet to learn about you, not just your site. The greater the number of independent sources that back up your site’s claims, the more likely these platforms are to mention them in responses. Your website may also become an AI citation source if third-party sites link to it, increasing its discoverability and authority. For example, if your latest product launch generates coverage and backlinks from multiple outlets, AI search platforms are more likely to mention it. This is because the third-party coverage indicates the launch is a verifiable, notable event. Some platforms may even cite your website as the information’s source alongside third-party ones. Two factors make a source especially credible to AI systems: Independence from the brand they describe : A claim about a brand made by a third-party source with little stake in the brand’s success holds more weight than an identical claim the brand makes on its own site Authoritativeness : Claims from authoritative sources are seen as deserving of higher weight because their information is often fact-checked and published by organizations with reputations to protect A digital PR strategy that gets authoritative third-party sources to mention your brand can thus do more than increase intangible brand awareness. It also builds the external evidence layer that AI search platforms use to understand and validate brands, translating into AI mentions and citations, plus other measurable visibility gains. The data that makes digital PR a viable AI visibility strategy Digital PR is a viable AI visibility strategy because third-party information sources have significant influence on how often AI search platforms mention and cite your brand, as the data shows. Take Patagonia. The outdoor clothing brand has over 87,000 AI mentions across platforms in the United States, according to our AI Visibility Index 2026 . The mechanism behind this high AI visibility: Patagonia’s presence on third-party sites Reddit, OutdoorGearLab, REI, SwitchbackTravel, GearJunkie, TreelineReview, and BetterTrail, which collectively mention Patagonia over 103,000 times. Similarly, Shopify has earned over 45,000 AI mentions across platforms. This strong visibility is the result of the ecommerce platform earning a significant volume of mentions on G2 (1,100+ mentions), Capterra (800+ mentions), Reddit (44,500+ mentions), LinkedIn (15,400+ mentions), and other third-party sites, per the same report. Earning mentions on the sources AI search platforms already favor is thus a clear path to stronger AI visibility for your brand. Where AI goes to decide who gets cited Since not all third-party sources carry the same weight, your PR targets should match the ones AI search platforms prefer to rely on. Here are the sources these platforms typically use to decide which brands to mention and cite: Encyclopedic/reference sources like Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Crunchbase Tier-one editorial and trade press like Forbes, Reuters, TechCrunch, and industry-specific publications, e.g., Modern Healthcare for the healthcare industry Review platforms like G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, and Trustpilot YouTube for official brand announcements and campaigns, and third-party product mentions and reviews Community forums like Reddit and Quora These sources’ importance varies by industry and brand. To find the exact sources that influence your brand’s AI mentions and citations, use a tool like Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit . Enter your domain into the tool, and then click “ Get started .” Scroll down to the “Topics & Sources” section and click “ Prompts ” to view prompts whose responses mention or cite your brand. Then, click “ View full response ” for any prompt to see the sources AI tools cited in their answer. Prioritize earning coverage from these sources with the digital PR tactics we’ll share next. Five PR moves that build AI visibility Use these five PR moves to grow your brand’s third-party record and build AI visibility at scale: 1. Original research: Turn proprietary data into publisher citations Publish proprietary data that publishers build stories around and cite. When publishers reference and link to the research’s source page on your site, the page gains authority, which makes AI search platforms more likely to mention and cite it. For example, Houzz published a 2026 U.S. renovation trends study that’s gotten over 180 backlinks from 81 referring domains, according to Semrush’s Backlink Analytics tool: AI search platforms have also cited the study’s source page on Houzz in more than 180 prompts, according to Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit . To turn proprietary data into publisher citations, create a research benchmark, survey, index, or trend report relevant to publishers’ beats. For instance, if your brand sells mattresses and you’re targeting citations from healthcare publications, you could publish a survey on your customers’ sleep patterns. Next, promote your research so publishers actually see and cite it. Share it on social media, and email it to publisher contacts you already have relationships with. Aim to publish new proprietary data every quarter. The more data you publish, the more publisher coverage and citations you might earn, driving higher AI visibility. 2. Third-party roundup placement: Get mentioned in the lists AI already uses Get mentioned in the product comparisons and roundup lists that AI search platforms cite. AI already trusts these pages, which means your brand is more likely to earn AI mentions if it’s featured on them. Product comparisons are pages that evaluate the pros and cons of two or more products (e.g., “QuickBooks Online vs Xero”). Roundup lists are pages that cover the best products in a category (e.g., “the best accounting software”) or alternatives to a product (e.g., “alternatives to QuickBooks Online”). AI search platforms tend to cite both types of pages when users ask for brand recommendations. For example, ChatGPT cited Fit Small Business’s roundup list in response to the prompt “Which is the best accounting software for small businesses in the US?”: In fact, ChatGPT cited this third-party list not once, but six times. And it didn’t cite the websites of its recommended brands at all. To get cited in the third-party product comparisons and roundup lists AI search platforms cite for prompts relevant to your brand, you first need to learn what these pages are. Use a tool like Semrush’s Prompt Research to help. Enter a topic relevant to your brand into the tool, and then click “ Analyze .” Scroll down to the “Related topics” section and click “ Prompts .” Next, enter one of these words into the “ Filter by prompt ” search bar: “vs” : to filter for product comparisons. To filter more specifically for product comparisons between your brand and a competitor, enter your brand’s name as well (e.g., “[your brand’s name] vs”). “best” : to filter for roundup lists for the best products in a certain category “alternatives” : to filter for roundup lists for alternatives to a product. To find pages that could feature your brand as an alternative to a competitor, add your competitor’s name to the filter (e.g., “[competitor’s name] alternatives”). Click the magnifying glass icon next to the search bar to apply the filter. Click “ View full response ” next to any prompt to see the response’s AI citations . Shortlist third-party pages where your brand could be a relevant addition. Then, reach out to their publishers about mentioning your brand on them. Don’t replace third-party validation of your brand with self-serving content on your site. For example, by publishing a roundup list that ranks your product as the best, followed by your competitors. This is because it’s the independence of third-party sources that makes their recommendations more credible and thus more worthy of AI citations. Publishing self-serving content might also inadvertently give your competitors more AI visibility than you. Google’s AI Overviews have been shown to cite a brand’s own comparison page or roundup list as a source, but recommend a competitor named within it instead, according to Lily Ray, Vice President of SEO & AI Search at Amsive . 3. Expert quotes: Get into cited industry coverage Get quoted as an expert in industry coverage that AI search platforms cite. They treat this coverage as a signal of authority and may be more likely to mention you as a result. Contributing expert quotes also helps these platforms learn about and mention your brand’s expertise to users, just like how Claude quotes Chef Mike Saperstein’s insights on searing meat: To maximize AI visibility, prioritize contributing expert quotes to journalists and publications that already appear as AI citations. Semrush’s Prompt Research helps you view these AI citation sources for prompts relevant to your brand. Alternatively, use expert-sourcing platforms like HARO to connect with journalists actively seeking quotes. When responding to quote requests, have relevant subject matter experts from your business provide clear perspectives and supporting data. Generic commentary is less useful — and less quotable — than specific, evidence-backed insights. 4. Review platform presence: Build corroboration beyond editorial coverage Build a presence on review platforms to help AI search platforms corroborate your brand’s positioning with what real users say about it. This independent corroboration, alongside other factors like brand authority and content quality, may help these platforms mention your brand more often. For example, software categories with 10% more reviews on review platform G2 tend to have about 2% more AI citations, according to an analysis by Kevin Indig, Growth Advisor and author of Growth Memo, published by G2 . Claiming a Trustpilot review profile can also increase AI citation rates from 1% to 54%, as a Trustpilot and Seer Interactive study found. Build a presence on review platforms that customers and AI search platforms use to research brands in your industry. For example, G2, Capterra, and Trustpilot are relevant review platforms for software products, while Yelp, Tripadvisor, and OpenTable are relevant for restaurants. To find review platforms relevant to your specific brand, use this prompt in ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI platform: “What do customers say about [brand]? Cite your sources.” If your brand’s online presence is low, use a close competitor’s name in the prompt instead. In the example below, ChatGPT heavily cited G2 while answering a prompt about customer reviews of Descript. So, if we were handling Descript’s digital PR, we’d focus on improving the brand’s presence on G2, among other review platforms. After shortlisting review platforms, create listings on each of them if you haven’t already. Check that your brand’s positioning on these listings matches that on your site to communicate a consistent picture of your brand to users and AI search platforms. If your brand operates physical stores, register Google Business Profiles (GBPs) for each store as well, because these profiles also display reviews. From there, consider connecting your GBPs to Semrush’s Listing Management to automatically create and update listings on multiple other review platforms. Once your listings are up, work on improving their review volume and recency, and the quality of your responses to reviews. Review data signals user sentiment toward your brand, which influences whether and how AI search platforms describe it to users. For example, get more reviews by sending automated post-purchase emails that ask for reviews, or creating QR codes for customers to scan to leave reviews. 5. Entity clarity: Reinforce core facts about your brand Work to make your brand’s core facts consistent across your site and authoritative third-party sources. Doing this helps AI search platforms recognize your brand as a standalone entity with certain distinguishable characteristics. They may then mention it more often. Audit your brand’s information on authoritative third-party sources AI systems routinely rely on for information. They include: Wikipedia Wikidata Crunchbase Google Business Profile LinkedIn YouTube Review platforms like G2, Yelp, and Tripadvisor These sources should all communicate the same essential facts about your brand, including its name, category, founding date, and product descriptions. They should also corroborate key claims, like whether your brand offers money-back guarantees. Edit your brand’s information on these sources if they’re inaccurate or missing certain details. And update them whenever your brand’s information changes. How to measure whether your PR is moving AI visibility Focus on metrics like citation lift, AI share of voice, and competitive citation displacement to measure whether your PR efforts move AI visibility instead of just placements. Here’s what each metric means: Citation lift : The percentage increase in AI citations of your brand across AI search platforms over time AI share of voice : The percentage of AI mentions of your brand in answers to non-branded prompts compared to competitors. Avoid tracking individual prompts. The phrasing variations are endless, so tracking each one is futile. It’s more useful to track your brand’s aggregate visibility across a broader prompt portfolio instead. Competitive citation displacement : Changes to the positions of AI citations of your brand and competitors Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit helps you track citation lift and AI share of voice. Enter your domain into the AI visibility tool , and then click “ Get started .” The Visibility Overview report shows your brand’s number of AI mentions, citations, and cited pages. It also displays these metrics: Trend charts over your selected time range Percentage changes over fixed periods (like against the previous month for the six-month view). This is helpful for measuring citation lift, for example. From there, scroll down and click “ Cited Pages ” to view which of your site’s pages have earned AI citations. Click any page to see the prompt and AI response that led to the citation. After identifying your top-cited content, revisit it every 60 to 90 days to maintain its freshness. AI search platforms favor referencing fresh content in their answers. Next, use the toolkit’s Narrative Drivers tool to view your brand’s AI share of voice. When you enter your domain into the tool, you’ll see two reports: Share of Voice : Your brand’s AI share of voice compared to competitors over time Share of Voice by Platform : Your brand’s AI share of voice compared to competitors in various AI systems Competitive citation displacement is an advanced AI visibility metric available in enterprise-grade tools like Semrush’s Enterprise AIO . It tracks AI citations for each prompt response, including changes to their positions over time, to help you monitor whether citations of your brand are rising while competitors’ fall. FAQs Does digital PR get AI to cite my website, or just mention my brand? Digital PR primarily helps with getting AI search platforms to mention your brand because these platforms favor surfacing independently corroborated claims. But digital PR can also increase the likelihood of these platforms citing your brand if the third-party coverage links to your pages, improving their discoverability and authority. How long does digital PR take to show up in AI answers? Digital PR might take anywhere from days to months to influence AI mentions and citations. AI search platforms that conduct live web searches may mention and cite new content within days of search engines indexing it. Platforms that rely solely on training data may update their mentions only when the companies behind them release new AI models. Which tools help measure digital PR’s impact on AI visibility? Tools like Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit and Enterprise AIO help measure digital PR’s impact on AI visibility. The AI Visibility Toolkit reports on citation lift and AI share of voice, while Enterprise AIO provides insights on competitive citation displacement. Sign up for a free trial or demo to explore their capabilities. Build your brand’s online record with digital PR AI search platforms trust what the internet says about your brand. Digital PR builds this record by earning mentions and citations from publishers, getting review platforms to corroborate your brand’s claims, and presenting a consistent picture of your brand across authoritative third-party sources. Leading brands are already locking in their AI mentions, citations, and shares of voice. Use Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit to establish your brand’s AI visibility baseline, because you can’t measure your digital PR’s effectiveness without one. title: Advancing the EV Static Wireless Charging Eco-System to the Next Level
body_text: Electrification and autonomous driving are two major trends reshaping the automotive industry at an unprecedented pace. Together, they revolutionize transportation by reducing emissions, enhancing safety, and providing a better user experience. McKinsey & Company predicts that worldwide demand for EVs will grow sixfold from 2021 through 2030, with annual unit sales increasing from 6.5 million to roughly 40 million. With the growth of electric autonomous vehicles, there is an immediate need for an electric vehicle charging infrastructure that enables charging without human intervention. Wireless charging for electric vehicles (EVs) promises a future where the hassle of plug-in is eliminated, making it an ideal solution for autonomous electric vehicle charging. Potential Challenges of Static EV Wireless Charging Imagine a robotaxi that requires charging; with wireless charging capability, it just needs to be parked on a charging pad, and it gets charged automatically without any human intervention. With the wireless charging market for electric vehicles expected to be worth $1,279 million by 2030, the profitability of wireless charging ecosystems cannot be denied. However, to reach a breakeven point the industry must overcome several challenges. Efficiency: Wireless charging typically exhibits lower energy transfer efficiency compared to wired charging, resulting in some energy loss as heat during the transfer process. Alignment Sensitivity: Precise alignment between the transmitter and receiver coils is crucial for optimal charging. Even slight misalignments can significantly reduce efficiency and increase charging time. Cost: The initial cost of wireless charging infrastructure, both for the ground-side and vehicle-side components, is currently higher than that of traditional wired charging systems. Electromagnetic Interference (EMI): The strong magnetic fields involved in wireless charging can potentially cause interference with other electronic devices. Careful shielding and adherence to safety standards are essential. Foreign Object Detection (FOD): Ensuring safety by detecting foreign objects, especially metallic ones, that may get between the charging pads is critical. These objects could heat up and pose a fire hazard. Heat Dissipation: The transfer of large amounts of power wirelessly generates heat, and effective heat dissipation systems are needed to prevent damage to components and ensure safety. Ongoing research and technological advancements are aimed at improving the efficiency, safety, and affordability of wireless EV charging systems. However, a highly streamlined strategy is what will make or break the entire ecosystem. Standardization as the Way Forward To ensure the successful implementation and broad acceptance of wireless EV charging, standardization plays a crucial role. The SAE J2954 Standard, with its comprehensive guidelines, is a crucial step towards addressing the challenges of wireless EV charging and paving the way for its broad acceptance. SAE J2954 is a standard for EV wireless power transfer, promoting the widespread adoption of wireless charging for EVs. It details the ecosystem for resonant inductive power transfer technology, primarily for static wireless charging. Key standardizations include ensuring interoperability between different EV models and charging stations, setting minimum efficiency requirements to reduce energy loss, defining charging levels up to 11 kW (with future support up to 500 kW for heavy vehicles), and implementing rigorous safety protocols. The standard also specifies alignment guidelines to ensure effective energy transfer even with slight misalignments. Together with ISO 5474-4:2025, which covers safety, power transfer efficiency, ground clearance, functionality, and interoperability for on-board vehicle equipment, these standards are pivotal in addressing the challenges of wireless EV charging and facilitating its broad acceptance. How to Build Standardized Components for EV Wireless Charging Building standardized components for EV wireless charging involves adhering to the guidelines set by SAE J2954 and ISO 5474-4:2025. The wireless power transfer system specified by SAE J2954 consists of two main parts: the Ground Assembly (GA), which is installed on the ground and transmits wireless power, and the Vehicle Assembly (VA), which is mounted under the vehicle and receives the power. Other key components include an alignment system for precise positioning and optimal power transfer, a communication system for data exchange and monitoring of alignment and safety, and power controllers in both assemblies to manage the conversion and transfer of electric energy, ensuring safe and efficient charging. ISO 5474-4:2025 too defines the requirements and operations of on-board vehicle equipment for magnetic field wireless power transfer (MF-WPT) between supply devices and electric vehicles (EVs). By following these steps and adhering to these standards, manufacturers can build standardized components that ensure interoperability, efficiency, and safety in EV wireless charging systems. This standardization is crucial for the widespread adoption and success of wireless charging technology in the automotive industry. Benefits of Standardization in EV Wireless Charging Standardization in EV wireless charging brings numerous benefits, ensuring the technology is efficient, safe, and widely adoptable. Here are the key benefits: Interoperability: Compatibility: Standards like SAE J2954 ensure that different EV models and wireless charging stations are compatible, promoting a streamlined and user-friendly experience. Functionality: ISO 5474-4:2025 ensures that on-board vehicle equipment can reliably function with off-board charging systems from different manufacturers, enhancing user convenience. Efficiency: Energy Transfer: SAE J2954 sets minimum efficiency requirements to reduce energy loss during wireless power transfer, improving overall system performance. It supports power levels up to 11 kW with an efficiency of up to 93%. Power Transfer: ISO 5474-4:2025 defines requirements for power transfer and efficiency, ensuring optimal charging performance. Charging Levels: Variety: SAE J2954 defines three classes of charging speeds (WPT 1, 2, and 3) at a maximum of 3.7 kW, 7.7 kW, and 11 kW, respectively. It also prepares for future support up to 500 kW for heavy electric vehicles. Safety: Protocols: SAE J2954 includes rigorous safety protocols to mitigate risks associated with electromagnetic fields (EMI), foreign object detection (FOD), and heat dissipation. Requirements: ISO 5474-4:2025 sets stringent safety standards to protect users from potential hazards like electromagnetic field exposure and heat generation. Alignment Guidance: Precision: SAE J2954 defines specifications for alignment tolerance to ensure effective energy transfer even with slight misalignments. It includes the Differential Inductive Positioning System (DIPS) strategy for accurate vehicle alignment, ensuring optimal charging efficiency. Ground Clearance: Compatibility: ISO 5474-4:2025 specifies requirements for the ground clearance of the vehicle's receiver unit, ensuring compatibility with various charging pad installations. Test Procedures: Verification: ISO 5474-4:2025 outlines standardized test procedures to verify compliance with its requirements, ensuring consistent performance and safety. By adhering to these standards, the EV industry can achieve a more seamless, efficient, and safe wireless charging ecosystem, ultimately contributing to the broader adoption and success of electric vehicles. Paving the Way for Efficient and Widely Adopted Wireless EV Charging In summary, the journey towards efficient and widely adopted wireless EV charging is marked by both technological advancements and significant challenges. The development and implementation of standards like SAE J2954 and ISO 5474-4:2025 are crucial for ensuring interoperability, safety, and efficiency in this emerging field. As the automotive industry continues to evolve with the rise of electric and autonomous vehicles, the advancement of wireless charging systems will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of transportation. By addressing current challenges and leveraging innovative wireless power transfer technologies, we can anticipate a more seamless and convenient electric vehicle ecosystem, ultimately contributing to a sustainable and efficient future. body_text: View All News Sensient Technologies Corporation Reports Results for the Quarter Ended June 30, 2026 July 24, 2026 Download (opens in new window) MILWAUKEE--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Sensient Technologies Corporation (NYSE: SXT), a leading provider of flavors and colors for the food, pharmaceutical, and personal care markets, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second Quarter Consolidated Results Reported revenue increased 11.6% to $462.1 million in the second quarter of 2026 versus last year’s second quarter results of $414.2 million. On a local currency basis (1), revenue increased 9.9%. Reported operating income increased 32.9% to $76.7 million compared to $57.7 million recorded in last year’s second quarter. In the second quarter of 2025, the Company recorded $3.3 million of costs related to its Portfolio Optimization Plan versus no costs recorded in the second quarter of 2026. Local currency adjusted operating income (1) and local currency adjusted EBITDA (1) were up 23.4% and 20.8%, respectively, in the second quarter. Reported earnings per share increased 36.4% to $1.20 in the second quarter of 2026 compared to 88 cents in the second quarter of 2025. Local currency adjusted diluted EPS (1) increased 25.5% in the second quarter. “Sensient continued to build on an outstanding first quarter. We are entering the second half of the year with great momentum and confidence in the future. By executing on our strategy, we are poised to take advantage of opportunities in the market and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. I remain very confident about our performance in 2026 and beyond,” said Paul Manning, Sensient’s Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer.
